second_order: Finding somewhere an LSU logo can stick
theme_note: These codes all choose, check, abandon, or revise a place for an LSU mark. What varies is whether people look for quiet or empty space, reuse purple, resize the plan to fit, or propose taking a rival's space.
regrouped_from: grouping review: split from negotiating with neighbors because these passages primarily choose or revise the site, even when another picture makes a site usable or unusable

second_order: Drawing and adjusting the purple-and-gold mark
theme_note: These codes turn an idea into a workable pixel design and lay down its frame, colors, blocks, letters, or border. They vary from choosing Toonces versus letters to adjusting widths and building the background.
regrouped_from: grouping review: split from rallying more hands because these passages do the design and pixel work rather than summon participants

second_order: Rallying more hands to finish or save it
theme_note: These passages commission the LSU mark, ask for help, recruit another person, or issue urgent calls to finish or save it. The calls range from an initial invitation to all-hands and emergency appeals.
regrouped_from: grouping review: split from drawing the mark because recruiting participation is a shared practice across initial building and later rescue calls

second_order: Working out room and help with neighboring groups
theme_note: These codes directly negotiate, offer help, set non-attack terms, or seek coexistence with neighboring school and interest-group pictures. What varies is the result: Wisconsin offers space and defense, hawks and Team Liquid work through overlap, Big10 refuses room, Rutgers arrives too late, and NYU challenges LSU's pixels.
regrouped_from: grouping review: split from finding a site and from naming displacement because these passages address or answer another group about sharing space or helping

theme_note: These passages fix pixels, watch logos, reclaim a place, maintain letters, and join a defense. They vary between routine watching of two logos, repair under active pressure, and hours-long attempts that ultimately lose one location.
regrouped_from: grouping review: split from naming who pushed LSU out because these codes describe participants actively maintaining or reclaiming the mark

second_order: Naming who is taking or threatening the spot
theme_note: These passages identify claims, overwriting, expected replacement, takeovers, and bullying that make an LSU site precarious. What varies is who is cast as the threat and whether LSU is the target or someone proposes making another school's picture the target.
regrouped_from: grouping review: split from keeping the mark up because reporting or blaming a threat is not the same practice as placing repair pixels

second_order: Showing, crediting, and cheering what LSU got down
theme_note: These codes display a result, thank or credit contributors, claim individual labor, and celebrate that a small group left a clean LSU mark. They vary between collective 'we did it,' individual credit, simple cheers, and preserving the image after the canvas closed.
regrouped_from: grouping review: kept collective celebration and individual credit together because both make and circulate an account of who produced the surviving result

second_order: Keeping LSU from turning into LSD — and joking when it does
theme_note: These codes concern the repeated alteration of LSU to LSD: asking for defense, recounting repairs, and turning the alteration into a joke. The practice shifts from live maintenance to post-event retelling and humor.
regrouped_from: grouping review: split from general defense because the same named alteration becomes both a repair problem and a shared post-event joke

theme_note: Both codes propose a schoolwide Discord as useful and move from asking whether one exists to offering to create it. No passage shows that anyone actually moved organizing there.
regrouped_from: grouping review: retained as a single-code-pair practice because proposing a new venue belongs with none of the on-canvas or subreddit coordination practices
